sentences.text: The type species, Paralligator gradilifrons, could reach a maximum length of four meters.
Its braincase reveals cerebral hemispheres roughly 2.5 times wider than the olfactory tract, suggesting a highly developed sense of smell relative to its brain size.
Unlike modern crocodilians that can breathe with their heads submerged, this animal likely had to lift its entire head out of the water to breathe.
The genus was established in 1954 when Konzhukova described Paralligator gradilifrons as the type species.
Later research in 2015 saw Turner classify the species P. ancestralis as a junior synonym of P. gradilifrons.
Its teeth were specifically adapted to crush bivalves, gastropods, and other shelled or exoskeleton-bearing animals.
Because its skull morphology does not suggest it was an ambush predator, researchers hypothesize its diet consisted of aquatic invertebrates.
Paralligator belongs to the family Paralligatoridae.
Three species previously classified in the genus Shamosuchus are now considered synonyms of Paralligator.
Paralligator lived in Mongolia during the Late Cretaceous, between 96 and 70 million years ago.
Fossil evidence places its habitat in the Gobi Desert of Mongolia during the Upper Cretaceous.
More precise dating indicates it lived from the Cenomanian to the Santonian stages, between 100.5 and 83.6 million years ago.
